title: Convertible Top: Finding the Frame Parts and Controls
introduction:
This component map covers the convertible top. I use the exposed-frame view for the roof structure, tension parts and seals, then the vehicle view for the switch and sensor locations. Think folding tent with a control system: fabric support and electrical feedback have different jobs, even when they live inches apart.

Each drawing has its own callouts and matching table, so restart with the appropriate table when changing views. The colored insets enlarge individual parts; their colors distinguish components rather than reporting a fault. This is a location guide, without operating, adjustment, removal or electrical-test instructions.

edits.text: Roof Frame, Tension Parts and Seals
edits.why: Start at the front panel and trace the exposed framework rearward. The long stay pads run along the roof sides over the bows; the floating bow forms the rearward curved frame member. The tension cable is routed through the top material, whereas the tension belt is located in the luggage compartment. The rear glass tension rod and the side-mounted motor are enlarged separately. Compare the seal insets by their table names: the rear panel lower seal, center panel side weather-strip sections and front panel side weather-strip occupy different portions of the roof. MRCMA means movable roof control module A, and MRCMB means movable roof control module B; retain those identifiers when discussing the motor entry. The motor row prints “MRCMA - LH side, MRCMB - side) RH”. The final RH may be a displaced word intended for the MRCMB label, but the page does not settle that reading. I leave the original row visible and do not use this uncertain label to identify a side-specific replacement motor.

Use the vehicle view to connect the overhead-console open/close switch with the front-header and rear-cover locations. The tonneau cover includes the magnet used to operate its sensor; the rear inset shows the sensor as part of the D-tower cover assembly, identified as PIA in the table. At the windshield header, the LH front striker contains the top latch switch. LH means left-hand and RH means right-hand. These locations help distinguish a switch, its associated mechanical part and the cover-mounted sensor; they do not establish test pinouts or authorize dismantling.

readerOutcome: Navigate the convertible-top component maps while recognizing that the malformed motor-side label remains uncertain and cannot identify a side-specific replacement.
teachingNotes: Both requested headings remain concise titles; component teaching sits in their why fields.
